suggestions.title: Close confirmation can rest on a stale first sighting when the reads in between were skipped or unreadable
suggestions.failurePath: Token mode. Sweep at t0 reads PR closed during a close/reopen to rerun CI, so closedSeenAt=t0 (line 675). The PR is reopened at t0+5s. A verify step is then claimed and runs for 15 min, so every sweep returns at the hasActiveStep check (line 482) before any read. closedSeenAt survives because liveKeys keeps the key (line 481). Unreadable reads also return at line 511 without touching it. After the verify step ends, the person closes and reopens again to rerun CI, and the next read lands in the closed window. readAt - seen is about 900 s, which is at least CI_CLOSED_CONFIRM_MS, so lines 679-682 write the closed row, set build.errorMessage, stop the unclaimed gate steps and move the card to failed. Two transient closes, with no open read between them, fail the card. That is the case the 50 s rule ([51]) is meant to prevent. The same holds in anonymous mode, where reads are 5 min apart. The odds are low and a person can recover the card (#702 restore or restart), so this is a suggestion. Fix: require the confirming read to come right after the closed read, for example by keeping the time of the last read and clearing closedSeenAt on skipped or unreadable sweeps.

suggestions.title: Containment check only looks at build-step checkpoints; a Verifier commit pushed after a GitHub merge finishes the card silently
suggestions.failurePath: The daemon commits and pushes for every step except review (apps/daemon/src/runner.ts:461 isReview; commitAll and push run for verify steps). The checkpoint query keeps only kind='build' done steps (lines 574-586). Path: the PR is merged on GitHub at head C1, which is the last build checkpoint, while a verify step is claimed and running. The verify step then pushes evidence commit V to the conversation branch after the merge. The next sweep has no active step: the pull is merged, headSha=C1 equals the checkpoint, so the code skips compare and finishes the card done. No hint is written and V never reaches the default branch. Spec 02 and the PR body describe the rule as 'the merge missed later work'. Either include verify-step checkpoints in the containment check, or say in spec 02 that only build-step commits count.

suggestions.title: finishTodoDone's already-done branch is unreachable from production callers, and test ㉟ pins behavior production does not have
suggestions.failurePath: completeStep returns early for a done card (builds.ts:1647, hasLeftExecution includes 'done'). It only marks the step done and writes no completion row. The reconcile calls finishTodoDone only after freshReviewRow confirms 'review'. So the current==='done' exemption at line 1893 and the republish at 1899-1902 never run in production. pr-reconcile.test.ts ㉟ ('the merge step completes after a manual done: completion row written') calls finishTodoDone directly on a done card and asserts a DONE_ROW. A real merge step that completes after a manual done writes no such row. Either drop the dead branch, or rename the test and drive it through completeStep so it pins the real behavior.

suggestions.title: Sweep tally misses cards held by an already-written hint
suggestions.failurePath: A merged PR into a non-default base (lines 562-570), or one whose head does not contain the checkpoint (lines 641-655), goes through hintOnce. On later sweeps hintOnce returns early because the row is already known (line 411), and the caller returns without counting the candidate in any bucket. reviewCandidates therefore exceeds the sum of reviewPending, reviewSkipped, reviewUnreadable, reviewForeign, merged, closedUnmerged, hinted and settledBefore on every sweep while such a card stays in review. That breaks the [55] intent of a sweep log that accounts for every reconcile candidate. This only affects logging: add a bucket (or count these under settledBefore or hinted) whenever the hint already exists.

suggestions.title: The base.ref/default_branch guard at ci-loop.ts:557-561 is reached by no test; ㉗ and [61] 'base' return earlier at line 532
suggestions.evidence: PullsMock (pr-reconcile.test.ts:264) sends `base: spec.noBase ? undefined : {...}`, so noBase removes base.repo.id along with base.ref and default_branch. The only option that keeps base present is noBaseRepoId. No PullSpec option drops base.ref or default_branch alone; every test passes strings or the 'main' default. ㉗ (test line 1108) and [61] 'base' therefore stop at ci-loop.ts:532 (`pull.baseRepoId === null`) and never reach line 557. r15-mutations M2d confirms it: ㉗ goes red only through the foreign-hint path. gates-15.txt states 'lines 557-561 return before that hint when baseRef or defaultBranch is null (㉗ and [61] 'base' pin it)', which is not what the tests exercise.
suggestions.failurePath: Mutation: delete `pullCache.delete(key);` at line 558, or change the counter on that branch. All 125 tests stay green and typecheck still passes, since the narrowing for githubText stays. In production, a merged response that has base.repo.id but no base.ref/default_branch would then stay cached with its ETag. Every later sweep gets a 304 for the same incomplete body and counts the card unreadable until restart. That is the round-13 [61] defect, now for these two fields, with no test to catch it. Fix: add noBaseRef / noDefaultBranch options to PullSpec that keep base.repo.id, and point ㉗ and the [61] 'base' case at them.

suggestions.title: The ci-loop batch-sweep test fails about 0.3% of runs from random PR-number collisions; likely the 'unexplained' round-11 failure
suggestions.evidence: addCandidate picks `prNumber = 100 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 900)` (line 266), and every CheckRunsMock defaults to etag '"etag-1"' (line 76). The grind cache key is `${target.fullName}#${prNumber}` (ci-loop.ts:708), and all addCandidate projects use githubRepo 'octo/demo'. The batch test '批量对账：3 候选一轮' (line 353) seeds three candidates. The PR body says one run in round 11 failed 'the batch sweep test' and the failure 'is not explained'. This exists on main too, since the cache key and the helper are unchanged in substance; the PR only adds latestBuildId to the helper.
suggestions.failurePath: When two of the three random PR numbers match (1 - 900*899*898/900^3, about 0.33% per run), the first candidate fills the cache entry. The second sends if-none-match '"etag-1"' to its own mock, gets a 304 and reuses the first candidate's verdict. The green candidate can then get a fix step instead of moving to review, and the test asserting 'review' fails. Fix: give addCandidate distinct PR numbers, for example a counter, or give each mock its own etag.

suggestions.title: Per-merge test results claimed after rounds 13/14 have no archived output
suggestions.failurePath: The Verified section claims results for the merges of main: '123 of 123 on the merge [4f71b7a] and typecheck passes', and 'the related server tests passed on each merge' for 0f35851 and 4237afa. No file under docs/verify/1403/ holds those runs, so a reviewer cannot check them. There is no gap at the head: gates-14.txt (fb06b51) and gates-15.txt (c6cf10b) ran the full gate set on trees that already contain all three merges, and I reproduced the narrow vitest, typecheck and lint at the head. Either drop the per-merge numbers or point to gates-14/15 as the evidence.
suggestions.evidence: PR body paragraph beginning 'After round 13 the branch took main at `4f71b7a`'. `ls docs/verify/1403` has no merge-run file.

suggestions.title: End-to-end leg (real server, PR merged on GitHub, card moves to done) has no evidence yet
suggestions.failurePath: The evidence has three parts. First, unit tests drive createCiPoller with a stubbed githubFetch; scheduler.ts:72-74 and :185-189 start this same poller on the 60 s interval. Second, response shapes were captured live, but through a credentialed proxy (rate limit 15000), so they say nothing about the anonymous budget path. Third, mutation runs. Nothing shows a running server moving a review card to done or failed from a real GitHub read. The PR states this openly: the Acceptance host leg is unchecked and deferred to spec 28 §8 / segment 3, and #1403 stays open. So this is not a gap in this segment's claims, but the anonymous-budget and live-sweep behavior remain unverified outside the test harness.
